turns.content: Hello, I'm your doctor today. What brings you in today?

Doctor: Hello, I'm your doctor today. What brings you in today? Patient: I’ve noticed gradually developing patches of lighter skin on my hands and face over the past few months. They’ve been expanding slowly, and they don’t itch or hurt.
Have you noticed any other skin changes—such as new darkening/whitening elsewhere, scaling, or any changes in hair/eyebrows—or is it limited to the lighter patches on the hands and face?

Patient: Mostly it’s limited to those lighter patches on my hands and face, and I haven’t noticed scaling or any darkening elsewhere. My hair and eyebrows look normal, and there’s been no change in sensation in the areas.
Do you have any history of sun exposure worsening the patches, or do they appear more noticeable after being outdoors?

Patient: It seems to be about the same whether I’m indoors or outdoors, though I do notice it more when my skin looks darker after being out in the sun. I haven’t had any major sunburns or clear flare-ups right after I’m outdoors.
Have you noticed any similar patches in other body areas (e.g., around the mouth, genitals, or underarms), or is it strictly hands and face?
Patient: It’s strictly limited to my hands and face—no patches around my mouth, genitals, or underarms, and I haven’t noticed anything else in those areas.
Have you started any new medications or supplements in the past 6–12 months (including antibiotics, steroids, or immune-related drugs)?
Patient: No, I haven’t started any new medications or supplements—no antibiotics, steroids, or immune-related drugs in the past year.
Have you had any recent infections, fevers, weight loss, or symptoms like diarrhea or abdominal pain?

Patient: No, I haven’t had any recent infections, fevers, weight loss, or stomach symptoms like diarrhea or abdominal pain. I feel otherwise healthy, aside from the slowly expanding lighter patches on my hands and face.
Do you have any family history of autoimmune diseases or skin conditions (like vitiligo), or have you ever been diagnosed with an autoimmune condition yourself?

I don’t have any known family history of autoimmune diseases, and no one in my family has been diagnosed with vitiligo or other similar skin conditions. I’ve never been diagnosed with any autoimmune condition myself.
Have you noticed any rapid progression (weeks) or is it truly slow over months, and are the borders of the patches well-defined or more diffuse?
Patient: It’s truly slow over the past few months—nothing that felt rapid in just a few weeks. The borders are fairly well-defined rather than diffuse, and the patches gradually expand outward.
Any history of skin trauma or friction to those areas (e.g., burns, chemical exposure, repeated irritation), or do the patches appear in areas without prior injury?

Patient: I haven’t had burns, chemical exposure, or repeated irritation there, and the patches seem to appear on skin that was previously normal. I don’t recall any specific trauma or friction that would explain the areas showing up.
Do you have any history of thyroid disease or symptoms such as heat/cold intolerance, palpitations, unexplained weight change, or fatigue?
I haven’t been told I have any thyroid problems, and I don’t have heat or cold intolerance, palpitations, unexplained weight change, or unusual fatigue.
Have you noticed any nail changes (pitting, discoloration) or oral/genital mucosal sores?
I haven’t noticed any nail pitting or discoloration, and I don’t have any sores or unusual spots in my mouth or genital area.

[ABSTAIN] The history is suggestive of a chronic depigmenting process (e.g., vitiligo), but the interview lacks key discriminators such as presence of depigmentation on Wood’s lamp, any autoimmune symptoms/labs (thyroid disease, diabetes, anemia), and whether there are any subtle associated findings (hair whitening, nail/oral involvement).  

[POSSIBLE] Vitiligo, Minimal Change Disease, Histoplasmosis, Toxic exposure, Steven-Johnson syndrome
